review: Astra core implemented 30 real Kernel/SQLite cases and passed a 147-case live focused regression. Independent Astra native review added 41 cases including eight fault cases with real SQL guards and explicit hook-hit assertions. Root verified 23 renderer cases including three real workbench/parent journeys, exact actor versus authentication key, body-free recovery and permission/expiry cleanup. Final results above come only from isolated frozen source.
boundaries: Explicit goal.memory.read/write/delete remain independent of generic goal.read/update. Every call needs goal.read and the relevant current memory permission; delete recovery can use delete-only rights. Creator DID is attribution, actual member is the execution actor.

Existing ContextMemoryKernel and NativeSqliteMemoryPort own bodies/lifecycle. Organization store+org+mapping+project+goal namespace is shared across members and isolated from personal/other-goal scopes. Bodies never enter goal records, operation journals or lifecycle events.

New mutation nonce validates and previews before default-cancel native confirmation, pins full current authority and rechecks before journal/Kernel. Cancellation records no mutation. Confirm includes source version, input digest, retention and exact actual actor.

Shared goal memory epoch and versioned links fence output. Final host revalidates output token against actual actor, current authority, scope, goal revision/control generation, epoch and exact Kernel references; stale grants/references cannot expose bodies.

Actor+goal+nonce operation journals hold input and Kernel fingerprint digests, admission authority attribution and body-free results. Members share authorized content but cannot recover/discard another actor operation; current permissions are checked on explicit recovery.

Goal-reference CAS, grants, shared epoch and operation receipt commit together. Eight independent native SQL fault cases hit actual writer guards and prove rollback or persistent deny as appropriate; Kernel body may commit first but has no output grant until successful goal transaction.

Lost proposal/supersede/reply/goal receipt recovers the original Kernel identity without new confirmation or write. Missing body never reconstructed from metadata. Revoke/delete deny first; partial deletion uses Kernel reconciliation and actual purged evidence, not elapsed time.

After verified goal completion, revoke/delete keeps original completion proof and historical references unchanged while independent grant blocks bodies. Memory facts/inferences/notes never prove task or goal completion.

Renderer clears bodies/drafts on invalidation, parent refresh, identity/scope/permission changes, grant/retention expiry and late output. Parent recovery contains only operation IDs, survives same-session refresh/revision, and never contains submitted body. Visible content rechecks authority at most every 30 seconds.

Windows selected native SQLite, Kernel, Vue, workbench and scheduler tests; Electron dialog/auth/window and test ACL callbacks injected. No full repository/full type checking/real Electron GUI/exact-commit Linux/macOS release matrix/real tenant business acceptance.

No automatic model/context injection and no additional memory engine. Local digests prove consistency, not independent signatures. Other actions, auxiliary/board paths and the remaining roadmap continue; no push or release.
